entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since late September 2026):

---

- 
**GRPM Anishinaabek exhibit reopened, Oct. 12, 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum reopened its redesigned "Anishinaabek: The Original People of This Place" exhibit, featuring new holographic visuals, hands-on experiences and immersive interior design after two years of renovations.
 
The exhibit also displays three new murals created by West Michigan Indigenous artists
, and 
includes a Veterans Wall of Honor built after years of collaboration between museum staff and Indigenous leaders.
 (WOOD TV / Hoodline)

- 
**"Frontier to Freedom" wins 2026 State History Award, Oct. 2, 2026:** The Historical Society of Michigan awarded *Frontier to Freedom* its 2026 State History Award in the Media category; producers Keith Patterson, Kevin Foley and David Van Hoof were honored at the HSM Awards Banquet held Sept. 25, 2026, at the Grand Rapids Public Museum.
 (The Sun Times News)

- 
**GRPM Archives opened to the public, Sept. 16, 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum opened a new public space at its Archives facility, making it a more accessible destination for students, educators, researchers and community members; the archives house over 250,000 artifacts and specimens, approximately 95% of the museum's total collections.
 (WWMT / WOOD TV)

- 
**Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids issue formal call for GRB federal recognition, Sept. 16, 2026:** The Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids publicly declared support for reaffirming federal recognition of the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians, noting the tribe has been working toward recognition for nearly 30 years.
 (Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids)

- 
**GRB federal recognition status unchanged as of October 2026:** The Cherokee One Feather's October 2026 monthly update confirms the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians remain in the federal acknowledgment process with no new congressional hearing scheduled on either the House or Senate recognition bills.
 (Cherokee One Feather, Oct. 21, 2026)

- 
**Michigan Historical Commission to consider language for GRB Footpath historical marker, November 2026:** The Michigan Historical Commission is scheduled to meet in November to consider language for the historical marker to be installed at the Grand River Bands Ottawa Indians footpath site in Eastown, Grand Rapids.
 (Grand River Bands website)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or recently changed items from approximately the last 30 days (since ~September 26, 2026), filtered against what was known as of August 1, 2026:

---

- **River North land RFQ issued, Oct. 7, 2026:** 
The City of Grand Rapids released a Request for Qualifications to select a development partner for a major mixed-use redevelopment of a nearly seven-acre site in the River North neighborhood, described as one of the most significant publicly owned redevelopment opportunities in the city's recent history.
 
Submissions are due Nov. 16, 2026; the city expects to select a partner in December or January.
 (City of Grand Rapids, Oct. 7, 2026)

- **Coldbrook site details confirmed, three parcels at Monroe Ave. NW:** 
The site includes the historic Coldbrook Pumping Station and the city's Development Center; the three parcels at 1101, 1165, and 1120 Monroe Ave. NW cover about 6.43 acres.
 
The city envisions a mixed-use development that could rise five to seven stories.
 
The fire department expects to move its training operations to a new facility by June 2027, clearing the way for that piece of the puzzle to move forward.
 (Grand Rapids Magazine, Oct. 11, 2026; Hoodline, Oct. 22, 2026)

- **City Q&A responses on River North RFQ posted today, Oct. 26:** 
Per the city's Economic Development page, responses to clarifying questions were posted Oct. 26, 2026, with the proposal submission deadline remaining Nov. 16, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. ET.
 (City of Grand Rapids, Oct. 26, 2026)

- **Canal Park renovation delayed to late fall 2026, new playscape name confirmed:** 
Canal Park at 905 Monroe Ave. NW is receiving a roughly $10 million renovation including a barrier-free canoe and kayak launch, river overlooks, and a new accessible play space called the Owashtanong Playscape, developed in partnership with the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians.
 
The project was originally expected to wrap up in spring but the timeline was pushed to fall, with the delay attributed to finishing the connective trail between Canal Park and the amphitheater site.
 (Kate Houseman blog, fall 2026)

- **Greenway: Cannonsburg Trail and Northland Tunnel both under construction, fall 2026 completion goal:** 
Per the Grand River Greenway project tracker (updated within the last 25 days), the Cannonsburg Trail (started summer 2026) and the Northland Tunnel (started spring 2026) both carry a fall 2026 completion goal, alongside Canal Park and the Oxford Trail.
 (Grand River Greenway network site, ~Oct. 2026)

- **Whitmer brownfield cap expansion, signed July 22, 2026, directly clears path for Grand Rapids projects:** 
The new law doubles the statewide cap on post-construction transformational brownfield tax captures from $1.6 billion to $3.2 billion, and Gov. Whitmer signed it

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~September 26, 2026):

---

- **Grand River Lower Reach restoration construction confirmed actively underway as of early October 2026:** 
A Construction Equipment Guide field report dated October 7, 2026 documented active boulder placement in the Grand River, with construction expected to span two seasons and conclude in fall 2027.


- **Michigan DNR Fisheries Orders 254 and 205 took effect September 10, 2026:** 
Regulation changes clarifying possession limits, identifying current fish communities, and aligning certain rules with Wisconsin were enacted by the NRC at its Sept. 9 meeting and became effective Sept. 10, 2026.
 These are not Grand River-specific but affect inland trout/salmon and Michigan-Wisconsin boundary waters statewide. No Grand River-specific fishing regulation changes were identified in this period.

- **No active flood watches, warnings, or public health water-contact advisories on the Grand River at Grand Rapids as of mid-September 2026:** 
NOAA's gauge at Grand Rapids reported no watches, warnings, or advisories in effect as of September 17, 2026.


- **Michigan state investment of $89 million announced for river cleanup, reported October 18, 2026:** 
The state announced earlier in October that it is investing $89 million to clean up the Detroit, Kalamazoo, and other rivers statewide.
 Grand River is not named explicitly in this tranche but the broader context affects the region.

- **MDHHS 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guide (released June 8, 2026, pre-baseline but not yet in River Brain):** 
The guides cover 696 Michigan waterbodies; statewide, 60 guidelines were relaxed and 64 became more protective compared to the prior year.
 
Grand River-specific advisories in the Southwest MI guide continue to flag PFOS in bluegill, rock bass, and sunfish, and PCBs in carp, with some "Do Not Eat" designations for rock bass upstream of Smithville Dam.
 No post-August 2026 changes to these advisories were found.

---

*No new EGLE permit actions specific to the Grand River in Grand Rapids were found within the last 30 days. The EGLE whitewater permit (Dec. 2024) and construction contract (spring 2026) remain the operative documents, with in-river work ongoing under that authority.*

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~Sept 26, 2026):

---

- **River North riverfront RFQ launched, Oct. 7, 2026:** 
The City of Grand Rapids released a Request for Qualifications to select a development partner for a major mixed-use redevelopment of a nearly seven-acre site in the River North neighborhood.
 
Proposal submissions are due November 16, 2026, with city responses to clarifying questions posted today (Oct. 26).
 (grandrapidsmi.gov, Hoodline)

- **Lower Reach construction confirmed active with boulder placement, Oct. 7, 2026:** 
A Construction Equipment Guide field report dated Oct. 7 shows a Komatsu excavator placing boulders using natural stone to restore rapids and create varied habitat, with Taplin Group delivering more than 125 scattered habitat boulders.
 
Construction is expected to span two seasons and conclude in fall 2027, depending on water levels and weather.
 (Construction Equipment Guide)

- **Upper Reach environmental review timeline updated, fall 2026:** 
The Upper Reach phase, involving removal and replacement of the Sixth Street Dam (the region's first sea lamprey barrier), is still working through a federal environmental review, with a draft impact statement not expected until July 2027.
 (katehouseman.com)

- **Canal Park kayak launch and Owashtanong Playscape delayed to fall 2026:** 
Canal Park's kayak launch and Owashtanong Playscape at 905 Monroe Avenue NW are delayed but expected to open this fall.
 (katehouseman.com)

- **River North Coldbrook Pumping Station redevelopment detail confirmed, Oct. 11, 2026:** 
The 6.43-acre RFQ site includes the Coldbrook Pumping Station, a 1911 structure decommissioned in 2022 after more than a century of service, and the city is asking prospective developers to consider incorporating its historic façade.
 (Grand Rapids Magazine)

- **WMEAC Mayors' Grand River Cleanup completed, Sept. 19, 2026:** 
The 2026 cleanup removed 11,600 lbs of trash, with the Sept. 19 kickoff at Sixth Street Park drawing 500+ volunteers across 6 participating cities, cleaning 35 sites and 12+ miles of river.
 (WMEAC)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days, plus a few items from the past 90 days that post-date the August 1, 2026 base research cutoff and are directly relevant to the Grand River system:

---

- **Snuffbox mussel stocking, SE Michigan, October 2026:** 
About 7,500 captive-reared snuffbox mussels were released into three waters in southeastern Michigan, in a stocking announced by the Michigan DNR in late September 2026.
 
The stocking targeted the Huron and Clinton rivers and Cass Lake.
 
Per the October 7, 2026 report, 1,000 of the stocked mussels were tagged with unique physical ID tags glued to each shell.
 (Outdoor News, October 7, 2026)

- **Grand River fall salmon/steelhead run at peak, October 2026:** 
As of current tracking, the Grand River (Kent and Ottawa Counties) is showing a peak run with high confidence, with kings, coho, and steelhead present at 55°F water temperature and flow of 2,050 cfs, with peak expected to end around October 30.
 
A guide-service report from October 6, 2026 noted salmon have started their spawning process and a small push of steelhead entered rivers following needed rainfall.
 (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub / Werkman Outfitters, October 2026)

- **DNR adopts genetic "parentage-based tracking" for stocking evaluation, October 2026:** 
The Michigan DNR has begun using genetic testing to track the success of fish-stocking operations, with the goal of finding out if fish in a given waterway descended from stocked parents, helping the DNR determine if its stocking efforts are paying off.
 
The DNR spends about a third of its annual budget on fish rearing and stocking, totaling over $11 million in fiscal year 2024-25.
 (Michigan Public, October 15, 2026)

- **Sea lamprey barrier EIS and construction timeline update, July 2026:** 
The 6th Street Dam will not be removed until a new lamprey barrier is constructed, a project still being studied by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, with a project design not expected to be selected until approximately 2028.
 
The Lower Reach restoration's first phase will cost up to $26 million and is expected to continue through fall 2027.
 (Bridge Michigan / Spartan Newsroom, July 2026)

- **Grand River state-record gizzard shad, April 2026:** 
A new Michigan state-record gizzard shad weighing 4.45 pounds and measuring 20.3 inches was caught by Sedrick Neinhuis of Lowell while spincasting on the Grand River in Kent County on April 22, 2026.
 
This beat the previous record of 4.12 pounds set on Lake St. Clair in 1996.
 (Michigan DNR, May 7, 2026)

entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found from the past ~30 days (since late September 2026). All spring flood and drought/ice-jam events predating August 1, 2026, are excluded as already baselined.

---

- 
Grand River at Grand Rapids (USGS gauge 04119000) is reading **2.32 ft, falling at -9.0% over 24 hours**, well below flood stage; action stage begins at 12.00 ft, flood stage at 18.00 ft.
 No watches or warnings are in effect. (circa Oct 26, 2026, HowsYourRiver / USGS)

- 
USGS gauge data at Grand Rapids shows the gage height holding near **3.00 ft** as of Oct 5, 2026, with the provisional data series running from Sep 28 through Oct 5, 2026.
 (Oct 5, 2026, USGS Water Data for the Nation)

- 
Grand River at Lansing (USGS-04113000) recorded a gage height of **2.46 ft** on Oct 19, 2026, with a recent minimum of **2.41 ft** on Oct 14, 2026, both well below flood thresholds.
 (Oct 19, 2026, USGS Water Data for the Nation)

- 
Grand River at Jackson (USGS 04109000) was flowing at **87 cfs** with a gage height of **9.21 ft** as of Oct 20, 2026; a 5-day forecast projected flow dropping to roughly **79 cfs** by Oct 24, described as "drier than normal for the date."
 (Oct 20, 2026, SnoFlo / USGS)

- 
NWS Grand Rapids Area Forecast Discussion (issued Oct 22, 2026) carried key messages of "Dry and Mild with Morning Fog" with high confidence in tranquil, warmer-than-normal conditions through the weekend, and chances for rain returning next week.
 No river flood products were issued. (Oct 22, 2026, NWS Grand Rapids)

- 
As of today (Oct 26, 2026), RiverApp aggregated live readings show Grand River at Grand Rapids at **3.78 ft stage / 3,730 cfs**; at Ionia at **9.89 ft / 1,720 cfs**; and at Jackson at **9.11 ft / 75.5 cfs**.
 (Oct 26, 2026, RiverApp / USGS)

entries.title: Construction progress
entries.body:
Now let me search specifically for anything more recent (last 30 days, roughly late September to October 2026) on these topics.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (late September to October 26, 2026), post-August 1, 2026 base date:

---

- **Lower Reach construction milestone, early October:** 
Excavators were observed working in tandem to remove sandbags from the Grand River on Saturday, October 3, 2026
, confirming active cofferdam operations are progressing into the fall construction window. (Detroit News, Oct. 8, 2026)

- **First-season dam removal confirmed ahead of winter pause:** 
Crews began work July 1, installing a large cofferdam to isolate roughly half the river flow and removing the first low-head dam; Executive Director Matt Chapman expected two of the four dams in the downtown stretch to be removed by the end of summer.
 (CitizenPortal / Talking Michigan Transportation podcast, Sept. 30, 2026)

- **Rapids audible downtown for first time in over 100 years:** 
"For the 1st time in over 100 years, you can actually hear rapids roaring in Downtown Grand Rapids again," Chapman said.
 (CitizenPortal, Sept. 30, 2026)

- **Canal Park renovation on track for late fall 2026 completion:** 
A $7.5 million renovation of Canal Park is underway to create a universally accessible play space, an accessible kayak launch, river outlooks, seating terraces, and a multi-purpose pavilion, with completion expected in late fall 2026.
 (Experience Grand Rapids, Oct. 13, 2026)

- **Upper Reach EIS draft date now cited as July 2027 by multiple sources:** 
The Great Lakes Fishery Commission and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers are evaluating alternatives for the Upper Reach, with a draft EIS anticipated in July 2027; construction does not have a start date yet, pending the environmental review and a permittable design.
 (Awesome Mitten, Oct. 15, 2026) Note: one earlier source (Yahoo/Spectrum) cited June 2027 for the draft EIS; July 2027 now appears to be the more current and consistently cited target.

- **Michigan state river investment context:** 
The state announced earlier in October 2026 it is investing $89 million to clean up the Detroit, Kalamazoo, and other rivers
, situating the Grand River project within a broader statewide river restoration push. (Arkansas Online / AP, Oct. 18, 2026)

entries.title: History and culture
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~September 19, 2026):

---

- 
**GRPM "Anishinaabek" exhibit reopened, Oct. 13, 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum reopened its redesigned "Anishinaabek: The Original People of This Place" exhibit on October 13, featuring holograms, multimedia storytelling, and a Veterans Wall of Honor built through years of collaboration with Indigenous leaders.
 
The exhibit also includes three new murals created by West Michigan Indigenous artists.
 (WOOD TV8 / Hoodline)

- 
**Powwow opening celebration, Oct. 10, 2026:** Hundreds of Michigan tribal citizens and allies gathered at the Grand Rapids Public Museum for a powwow celebrating the Anishinaabek exhibit's reopening, filling all three floors of the museum.
 (Native News Online)

- 
**Dominican Sisters call for GRB federal recognition, Sept. 16, 2026:** The Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids publicly endorsed efforts to reaffirm federal recognition of the Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians, citing nearly 30 years of advocacy and lack of access to social services, education, housing, elder care, and treaty rights.
 (Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids)

- 
**GRPM Archives opened to public, Sept. 16, 2026:** The Grand Rapids Public Museum opened a newly renovated public space at its Archives facility, housing over 250,000 artifacts and specimens representing roughly 95% of the museum's collections.
 
The expansion includes classrooms, artifact labs, and meeting rooms; groundbreaking occurred in October 2025, supported in part by a $1 million State of Michigan grant.
 (WWMT / Fox 17 / Grand Rapids Magazine)

- 
**Federal recognition bills still in committee as of Oct. 12, 2026:** H.R. 3255 and Senate Bill 2160 (Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians Restoration Act of 2025) remain active but unscheduled for hearings, still awaiting committee action in the House Natural Resources Committee and Senate Indian Affairs Committee respectively.
 (Cherokee One Feather)

- 
**GRB Adult Duck Race and Ghost Supper, Oct. 25, 2026 (upcoming):** The Grand River Bands of Ottawa Indians have scheduled their 2026 Adult Duck Race and Ghost Supper for October 25 at Townsend Park Pavilion, Ramsdell Avenue NE, Cannon Township.
 (grandriverbands.com)

entries.title: Development and funding
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (post-August 1, 2026 base date), filtered to what is most recently confirmed:

---

- 
**River North Coldbrook site RFQ issued, Oct. 7, 2026:** The City of Grand Rapids released an RFQ to find a development partner for 6.43 acres of city-owned riverfront property in the River North neighborhood (three parcels at Monroe Ave NW and Coldbrook Street NW, including the historic Coldbrook Pumping Station).
 
Clarifying questions are due today, Oct. 19; proposal submission deadline is Nov. 16, 2026.
 (City of Grand Rapids, Wood TV)

- 
The city expects to select a development partner in December 2026 or January 2027.
 
The selected partner will lead a 12-month due diligence and master site planning process and, upon completion, receive a contractual right of first refusal to purchase the property.
 (City of Grand Rapids, Grand Rapids Magazine)

- 
**State brownfield cap doubled, July 22, 2026:** Gov. Whitmer signed legislation doubling the cap on post-construction transformational brownfield tax captures from $1.6 billion to $3.2 billion, "clearing a path for hundreds of millions of dollars in stalled projects" including downtown Grand Rapids.
 (Crain's Grand Rapids Business)

- 
**Canal Park and Johnson Park nearing fall 2026 completion:** A redesigned Canal Park is set to reopen in downtown Grand Rapids with a universally accessible, river-themed playscape, a barrier-free canoe/kayak launch, and river overlooks; riverfront Johnson Park will also open a new natural-surface trail for biking, hiking, running, and adaptive cycling this fall.
 (Experience Grand Rapids)

- 
**Fulton and Market construction start imminent:** The $740 million Fulton and Market mixed-use development, converting seven acres of surface parking at Fulton St. and Market Ave. into nearly 700 residences, a boutique hotel, and 53,000+ sq ft of retail, is scheduled to begin construction fall 2026, with completion targeted between fall 2028 and spring 2029.
 (Spectrum Local News)

- 
**Greenway investment total confirmed:** More than $150 million is being invested in the Grand River Greenway over the next two years.
 
Active under-construction Greenway projects currently include the Lower Grand River Water Trail, Grand River Restoration Lower Reach, Canal Park, Oxford Trail, and the Grand River Edges Trail (Leonard to Ann segment).
 (Experience Grand Rapids, Grand River Network)

entries.title: Regulations and advisories
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from approximately the last 30 days (since ~Sept. 19, 2026), plus one item from early October that is directly relevant to active construction status:

---

- 
Active Lower Reach construction ongoing as of Oct. 7, 2026: a Komatsu excavator with an NPK grapple is placing boulders in the Grand River; the two-season project is expected to conclude fall 2027 (Construction Equipment Guide, Oct. 7, 2026).


- 
Upper Reach planning update: the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers are evaluating alternatives, with a draft Environmental Impact Statement anticipated July 2027; no construction start date is set (Awesome Mitten, Oct. 15, 2026).


- 
Sea lamprey barrier status: the Sixth Street Dam will not be affected by Lower Reach construction; researchers are still evaluating options for maintaining lamprey protection as Upper Reach planning continues (Awesome Mitten, Oct. 15, 2026).


- 
Michigan DNR NRC regulation change effective Sept. 10, 2026: updated trout, salmon, and lake sturgeon rules under Fisheries Orders 254 and 205 are now in effect, including clarified possession limits and alignment of Michigan-Wisconsin boundary water regulations (Michigan DNR, Sept. 10, 2026).


- 
Canal Park renovation underway along the Grand River in downtown Grand Rapids: a $7.5 million project creating an accessible kayak launch, river outlooks, seating terraces, and an enclosed pavilion; completion expected late fall 2026 (Experience GR, Oct. 13, 2026).


No new MDHHS Eat Safe Fish advisories specific to the Grand River and no new EGLE permits were found within the last 30 days. The 2026 Eat Safe Fish Guide (released June 8, 2026) and the EGLE whitewater permit (issued Dec. 2024) remain the most recent entries for those categories, both predating the Aug. 1, 2026 base research date.

entries.title: Events and community
entries.body:
Now let me do a targeted search for the most recent (last 30 days, i.e., September 19 to October 19, 2026) news specifically.
Here are the genuinely new or changed items from roughly the last 30 days (since ~September 19, 2026):

---

- **River North riverfront RFQ issued, Oct. 7, 2026:** 
The City of Grand Rapids is seeking a development partner for nearly seven acres of city-owned property in the River North neighborhood, including the historic Coldbrook Pumping Station at Monroe Avenue and Coldbrook Street, through a newly released request for qualifications.
 
The RFQ was released Oct. 7; questions are due Oct. 19, an optional site visit is Oct. 20, and proposals are due Nov. 16.
 (Grand Rapids Magazine)

- **Lower Reach restoration construction update, Oct. 7, 2026:** 
Contractor Taplin Group LLC is actively placing boulders in the river; crews are removing four low-head dams and replacing them with two channel-wide grade-control structures built from rock and river material, plus more than 125 scattered habitat boulders and gently sloping riffles.
 
Construction is expected to span two seasons and conclude in fall 2027, depending on water levels and weather.
 (Construction Equipment Guide)

- **Michigan announces $89M statewide river investment, ~Oct. 2026:** 
The state of Michigan announced earlier this month it is investing $89 million to clean up the Detroit, Kalamazoo, and other rivers
, as part of a broader statewide push that includes the Grand River rapids restoration. (Northwest Arkansas Online, Oct. 18, 2026)

- **Canal Park renovation nearing completion, fall 2026:** 
The Grand River Greenway project includes Canal Park, where a $7.5 million renovation is underway to create a universally accessible play space, an accessible kayak launch, river outlooks, seating terraces, and a multi-purpose plaza with an enclosed pavilion; the renovation is expected to be completed in late fall 2026.
 (Experience Grand Rapids)

- **Grand River Greenway projects near fall/winter 2026 completion targets:** 
The Grand River Network projects page shows the South Rogue River Trail recently completed, and the Cannonsburg Trail (start: summer 2026, goal: fall 2026), Pettis Ave. Trail North (start: spring 2026, goal: winter 2026), Lower Grand River Water Trail (goal: 2026), and Grand River Edges Trail from Leonard to Ann (goal: fall/winter 2026) all currently under construction.
 (Grand River Network, updated ~Oct. 1, 2026)

- **Water rescue at 6th Street Bridge, Oct. 18, 2026:** 
Two fishermen were rescued from the Grand River on Saturday morning; around 7:30 a.m., crews were called to a water rescue by the 6th Street Bridge, where the two had stepped into a deeper section of the river.
 
The GRFD Water Rescue team launched a rescue boat from Fish Ladder Park; both fishermen were retrieved by boat and transported to the hospital.
 (WOOD TV8 / Yahoo News)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed items found since approximately August 1, 2026:

---

- 
Active dam removal on the Grand River downtown is underway as of October 2026: four low-head dams are being pulled and 30 acres of river corridor are being rebuilt with boulders to enhance aquatic habitat for lake sturgeon, river redhorse, and the federally endangered snuffbox mussel.
 (Oct 11, 2026, EcoPortal / Hugo Rojas)

- 
The Grand River salmon and steelhead run is currently at **peak** status with high confidence, with Kings, Coho, and Steelhead in the river at 55°F and 2,050 cfs (low and steady), with peak expected to end around Oct 30.
 (Oct 19, 2026, Michigan Fly Fishing Hub live tracker)

- 
As of Oct 6, 2026, salmon have begun their spawning process on the Grand River, prompting a shift to steelhead and trout fishing; recent rain pushed a small push of steelhead into the river and egg flows have begun, with trout and steelhead hitting almost exclusively an egg bite.
 (Oct 6, 2026, Werkman Outfitters fishing report)

- 
The Michigan DNR has begun using genetic "parentage-based tracking" to determine whether fish living in waterways descended from stocked parents, aiming to measure whether its multimillion-dollar stocking operations are producing self-sustaining populations.
 (Oct 15, 2026, Michigan Public)

- 
The Sixth Street Dam, which currently blocks sea lamprey from moving upstream into the Grand River, will not be removed until a new barrier is built; that replacement project is still being studied by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
 
A project design is not expected until approximately 2028, and more than $20 million in federal funding has already been secured for the future barrier.
 (Jul 31, 2026, Bridge Michigan / Spartan Newsroom)

- 
U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service applied lampricides to the Grand River in April 2026 to kill invasive sea lamprey larvae burrowed in the streambed.
 (Apr 11, 2026, Yahoo News / USFWS)

The exhibit also includes three new murals created by West Michigan Indigenous artists.

 This adds a new institutional voice to the ongoing recognition campaign. (Dominican Sisters of Grand Rapids, Sep 16, 2026)

*The Historical Archaeology of Michigan*, by Dean L. Anderson, Michael S. Nassaney, and Krysta Ryzewski, was published January 13, 2026 by the University Press of Florida; it brings together archaeological research across the state's last 400 years, including findings associated with Anishinaabe peoples.
 
The book highlights Anishinaabe peoples, settler colonialism, immigrants, agriculture, industry, and urbanization.
 (University Press of Florida / Michigan State Historic Preservation Office, 2026)

entries.title: Fish and wildlife
entries.body:
Here are the genuinely new or changed findings from roughly the last 30 days (since ~September 12, 2026), plus a few items from the past 60–90 days that post-date the August 1 baseline:

---

- **Snuffbox mussel, DNR stocking, Sept. 25, 2026:** 
About 7,500 captive-reared snuffbox mussels were released into three waters in southeastern Michigan, announced by the Michigan DNR in late September 2026; 1,000 of them carry passive integrated transponder (PIT) tags to enable RFID-based follow-up surveys.
 
Approximately 2,800 mussels went to the Clinton River, over 4,100 to the Huron River, and 500 to Cass Lake.
 Note: these are not Grand River sites, but the stocking program directly parallels ongoing Grand River snuffbox recovery work.

- **Lake sturgeon, genetics breakthrough, Sept. 28–30, 2026:** 
LSSU researchers refined a genetic testing method that makes sex determination in sturgeon more reliable, a useful tool for fisheries research, conservation, and aquaculture; findings were published Sept. 3 in BioTechniques.
 
The breakthrough could aid conservation and fisheries management by reducing handling time and allowing researchers to analyze archived samples.


- **Salmon and steelhead runs, Grand River, as of Oct. 12, 2026:** 
The Grand River (Kent and Ottawa Counties) is currently at peak run status, high confidence, for Kings, Coho, and Steelhead, at 60°F water temperature and 2,040 cfs flow, with peak expected to end approximately Oct. 12.


- **Invasive carp barrier, Sept. 29–30, 2026:** 
Great Lakes lawmakers argue that recent construction pauses are especially concerning after hundreds of juvenile silver carp were found just 80 miles from Lake Michigan, warning that an invasion could damage native fisheries, ecosystems, and billions of dollars in fishing and boating-related economic activity.
 
In July, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers paused work for the second time on the $1.15 billion Brandon Road Interbasin Project that aims to block invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes.
 
While that most recent stop-work order was lifted this month, legislators wrote that the delays are increasing the already hefty price tag of the project.


- **Sea lamprey barrier, Upper Reach EIS, Grand River, ongoing:** 
The 6th Street Dam will not be removed until a new lamprey barrier is constructed, a project still being studied by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; the GLFC aquatic connectivity coordinator stated a project design is not expected to be selected until approximately 2028.
 
More than $20 million in federal funding has already been secured for the future barrier project.


- **Invasive species, Grand River corridor, April–May 2026 (new since baseline):** 
Lesser celandine (*Ficaria verna*) is already widely established along the Grand River corridor and is actively spreading in Lower Michigan and southeastern Wisconsin.

Of those, 1,000 received PIT tags, 1,000 received physical shell tags with unique identifiers, and the remainder received color markings, allowing researchers to track survival, reproduction, movement, and impacts from invasive zebra and quagga mussels.

Michigan researchers refined genetic testing that can more reliably determine the sex of lake sturgeon, particularly in young fish and outside the spawning season, which could reduce handling time and allow analysis of archived samples for conservation and fisheries management.

The Grand River (Kent and Ottawa Counties) is currently at peak run status with high confidence, carrying kings, coho, and steelhead at a water temperature of 65°F and a flow of 2,690 cfs (low and steady); peak typically ends around Oct. 12.
 (Michigan Fly Fishing Hub, Oct. 7, 2026)

The USFWS Great Lakes Mass Marking Program shifted its emphasis from steelhead to coho salmon in 2025; yearling steelhead stocked in 2025 were mass-marked with an adipose fin clip and coded wire tag, but the 2026 stocking cohort was not subject to mass marking.
 
Around 90% of steelhead caught in Prairie Creek and the upper Grand have been wild fish in recent years.
 (Michigan Sea Grant / Great Lakes Angler Diary, Sep. 22, 2026)
